title: Allow emails up to 254 characters
bug: The email format check is gone: `not-an-email` is accepted.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR removed the Email() validator, so invalid email strings like 'not-an-email' now pass validation and create users (400->201), which the description did not announce.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR removed the Email() validator, so invalid email strings like 'not-an-email' now pass validation on PUT /api/me (400->200), which the description did not announce.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR removed the Email() validator, so invalid email strings like 'not-an-email' now pass validation and create users (400->201), which the description did not announce.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR removed the Email() validator, allowing creation of a user with invalid email 'not-an-email' (c1), which then enables successful login and token issuance (401->200), an unannounced consequence.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR removed the Email() validator, allowing creation of a user with invalid email 'invalid' (c1), which then enables authenticated access to GET /api/me (401->200), an unannounced consequence.

findings.detail: changed: html.forms.*.fields.required_field_2ab1 (removed), html.forms.*.fields.required_field_98dc (added), html.forms.*.fields.return_to, html.forms.*.fields.timestamp_secret, +1 more
findings.label: regression
findings.why: The reviewer suspected it, the twin confirmed it, and the PR description doesn't announce it. The OAuth2 GitHub HTML form field changes are unrelated to the email length change; insufficient context to determine if intended or regression.

findings.detail: changed: html.forms.*.fields.required_field_95b4 (removed), html.forms.*.fields.required_field_e46b (added), html.forms.*.fields.return_to, html.forms.*.fields.timestamp_secret, +1 more
findings.label: regression
findings.why: The reviewer suspected it, the twin confirmed it, and the PR description doesn't announce it. The OAuth2 GitHub HTML form field changes on a second round are unrelated to the email length change; insufficient context to determine if intended or regression.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR intentionally increases the email length limit to 254 characters per RFC 5321, but unintentionally removes email format validation, causing invalid emails to be accepted and cascading into successful user creation, login, and token issuance.

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed, allowing invalid email addresses to be accepted during user registration and password reset requests.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON body {"username": "testuser", "email": "not-an-email", "password": "password123"}. Expect HTTP 201 Created (previously 400 Validation Error). Read response JSON to confirm user created with invalid email.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 POST /api/users with invalid email returned base 400 validation error and head 201 Created with user created containing invalid email

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed, allowing invalid email addresses to be accepted during password reset request.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens/reset with JSON body {"email": "not-an-email"}. Expect HTTP 204 No Content (previously 400 Validation Error). Verify no email is sent by checking mail logs or mock.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 POST /api/tokens/reset with invalid email returned base 400 and head 400, both validation errors

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed, allowing invalid email addresses to be accepted when updating user profile.
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as a user, then send PUT /api/me with JSON body {"email": "not-an-email"}. Expect HTTP 200 OK (previously 400 Validation Error). Read response JSON to confirm email updated to invalid format.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 PUT /api/me with invalid email returned base 400 validation error and head 200 OK with email updated to invalid format

suspicions.claim: Email format validation is removed, allowing invalid email addresses to be accepted during OAuth2 user creation.
suspicions.trigger: Mock OAuth2 provider to return user info with invalid email (e.g., "not-an-email"). Complete OAuth2 flow with valid code/state. Expect HTTP 200 OK and user account created with invalid email. Verify by logging in with returned access token and checking /api/me response.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4: GET /api/tokens/oauth2/github changed: html.forms.*.fields.required_field_2ab1 (removed), html.forms.*.fields.required_field_98dc (added), html.forms.*.fields.return_to, html.forms.*.fields.timestamp_secret, +1 more; round2 probe_s4: GET /api/tokens/oauth2/github changed: html.forms.*.fields.required_field_95b4 (removed), html.forms.*.fields.required_field_e46b (added), html.forms.*.fields.return_to, html.forms.*.fields.timestamp_secret, +1 more

suspicions.claim: Gravatar avatar URLs generated from invalid emails may be malformed or unexpected due to missing email format validation.
suspicions.trigger: Create a user with invalid email (e.g., via POST /api/users with email "invalid"). Authenticate and send GET /api/me. Read response JSON field "avatar_url". Observe if URL contains unexpected hash or format due to invalid email input.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s5: POST /api/users status 400 -> 201; probe_s5: POST /api/tokens status 401 -> 200; probe_s5: GET /api/me status 401 -> 200

suspicions.claim: Password reset emails may be sent to syntactically invalid email addresses, causing delivery failures or bounces.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens/reset with JSON body {"email": "invalid-email"}. Expect HTTP 204. Check mail server logs or mock to verify send_email was called with invalid email address as recipient.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s6 POST /api/tokens/reset with invalid email returned base 400 and head 400, both validation errors, so reset email not sent
